caption: Research workflow and leakage-resistant evaluation design.
Selected balancing authorities: (a) mean demand by interconnection; (b) share of hours flagged by PUDL screening or missing, by year.
Normalised hourly demand of three BAs of different size and climate (validation year 2023; test data not shown).
PUDL screening codes by BA (2019–2025, sorted by mean demand). Flagged hours are excluded from scoring; model inputs use an independent causal screen.
Distribution of per-BA test nMAE (2024–2025) by method and horizon.
(a) Per-BA nMAE of the global model when the BA is held out vs included in training (colour: log10 mean demand). (b) Relative geographic generalisation gap vs BA size.
Temporal distribution shift: (a) median nMAE by year for models trained on 2019–2022; (b) by season (test period); (c) frozen vs refit models on 2025.
Limited target-data adaptation for unseen BAs: median test nMAE vs weeks of target history.
Calibration of nominal 90% intervals (h = 24 h): per-BA coverage (dots; bar = mean) for (a) in-region and (b) unseen-region models; (c) monthly pooled coverage for unseen BAs.
Day-ahead 90% prediction intervals for an unseen BA (IID), test period (BA chosen as the one with median CQR coverage).
Robustness to missing inputs: median test nMAE vs share of missing input hours for imputation strategies; × and + mark 24-h and 168-h outage scenarios.
Ablations of the zero-shot global model (h = 24 h): (a) feature groups (bars: median relative change; whiskers: 95% bootstrap CI over BAs); (b) size of the source-region pool.

Computational cost on a 4-core CPU: (a) wall-clock training time; (b) serialised model size (ridge size not measured). The h = 6 h in-region fit coincided with a concurrent evaluation job and its time is inflated by CPU contention; LRO fits at h = 6 h are representative.
